findings.reason: The original standalone tile renders the definition without a LaTeX defect, but the local covering construction identifies three concrete objects and a commuting triangle: the two chartwise sheets and their common base. A chartwise diagram materially clarifies that the involution changes the orientation ray while preserving the base point, including for boundary charts. This meets the expanded missing-diagram editorial criterion.

diagram_math_checks.objects: For the fixed chart phi:U -> V, U_+={(x,o_phi(x)):x in U} and U_-={(x,-o_phi(x)):x in U} are precisely the two local sheets specified in Definition line 42. Their disjointness follows from the two distinct positive rays in the one-dimensional determinant line.
diagram_math_checks.maps: tau|_{U_+}:U_+ -> U_- sends (x,o_phi(x)) to (x,-o_phi(x)); pi|_{U_+}:U_+ -> U and pi|_{U_-}:U_- -> U both send (x,±o_phi(x)) to x. Thus every displayed arrow has the indicated domain and codomain.
diagram_math_checks.relations: The triangle asserts (pi|_{U_-}) composed with (tau|_{U_+}) = pi|_{U_+}; both sides evaluate to x on every (x,o_phi(x)). The undrawn inverse tau|_{U_-} sends the negative ray back to the positive ray, and tau²=id follows from -(-o)=o.
diagram_math_checks.local_geometry: The local coordinates on each sheet are (x,±o_phi(x)) -> phi(x) by Definition line 42. Thus each restricted projection and its inverse have identity chart expression and are diffeomorphisms, also at the boundary. This diagram makes no global splitting claim and no overlap-sign or canonical-orientation assertion beyond the unchanged definition.
